title: Iquitos and the Rubber Boom: Regrets and Reproaches

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *debería haber* + participle from B2 Unit 10: the modal stays in the conditional and *haber* carries the past, so *Deberíamos haber viajado* means "we should have travelled". Said about yourself it is a regret, said about someone else it is a reproach. *Me arrepiento de* + *haber* + participle is a plain regret. Here you use it for your own trip and reading, and you keep judgements about history to attributed sources.

sections.title: At work on the topic
rows: Deberíamos haber viajado a Iquitos en barco.
Deberías haber visitado la Casa de Fierro.
Tendríamos que haber leído el informe antes.
Me arrepiento de no haber leído antes el informe de Casement.

items.spanish: Deberíamos haber llegado a Iquitos en barco, porque no hay carretera.
items.english: We should have arrived in Iquitos by boat, because there is no road.

items.spanish: Deberías haber visitado la Casa de Fierro en Iquitos.
items.english: You should have visited the Iron House in Iquitos.

items.spanish: Tendríamos que haber leído el informe de Casement antes del viaje.
items.english: We should have read Casement's report before the trip.

items.spanish: Me arrepiento de no haber leído antes el informe de Casement.
items.english: I regret not having read Casement's report earlier.

sections.content: The modal carries the person and the conditional (*deberíamos*); *haber* never changes and the participle never changes: *haber llegado*. Compare *Deberías visitar* (advice for now) with *Deberías haber visitado* (you did not).
